summary: Learn to set forecast triggers, pre-agree actions, map financing, and connect early assistance with social protection. Explore the five-day course.
lede: Anticipatory action connects forecasts and risk information to planned assistance before a hazard causes severe impacts. This training is for humanitarian programme managers, disaster-risk officials, social-protection teams and operations staff who need to turn forecast signals into workable plans. Participants practise setting trigger thresholds, structuring early action protocols, mapping pre-arranged financing and delivery roles, and linking actions to cash assistance and social-protection systems.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who plan, finance, coordinate, or deliver early assistance linked to forecasts, hazard impacts, and social protection systems. This course is designed for: Humanitarian programme managers coordinating forecast-triggered early action plans. Disaster-risk officials translating hazard forecasts into operational trigger decisions. Social-protection policymakers linking early action to existing transfer systems. Red Cross operations staff drafting and activating Early Action Protocols. NGO anticipatory-action coordinators assigning delivery roles before forecast thresholds are reached. Contingency-finance officers defining release conditions for anticipatory action. Humanitarian cash specialists planning pre-shock cash and voucher assistance. Early-warning analysts assessing forecast thresholds and impact information. Government programme planners aligning contingency plans with social protection caseloads. Donor programme officers reviewing trigger logic, financing, and delivery readiness.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Working familiarity with humanitarian programming, disaster-risk management, social protection, or contingency planning is recommended. No coding or programming is required; basic spreadsheet use will support the Excel-based trigger-monitoring exercise.
